minutes.headline: Assessors agreed to keep the senior 41C exemption article on the May warrant and sort out eligibility limits before town meeting.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard status reports from the interim and new principal assessors, then spent most of the meeting on a Clause 41C warrant article for elderly exemptions. Income and asset limits are inconsistent across records, and the board reached consensus to keep the article on the warrant and resolve eligibility later. They also covered delayed tax bills, citizen questions, and the next meeting date, then went into executive session on exemptions.

Welcomed the new assessor, praised the board, and asked that residents be updated on tax bill timing and abatement process via Facebook or the website.

budget_items.topic: Release of lien on rollback taxes, Holman Street
budget_items.what_was_said: Rollback taxes from 2022 were paid but the lien was never released after the prior assessor left; release to be signed.
Office list, DLS data bank, and town meeting records give inconsistent income and asset limits; the abatement amount is understood to be 750 since 2006 and a move to 1,000 and age 65 is proposed.
The budget requested a part-time data collector, only effective July 1 if town meeting approves; the board wants to plan for coverage gap.

decisions.decision: Consensus to keep the Clause 41C warrant article (raise exemption to 1,000, lower age to 65) on the May warrant and determine income/asset eligibility before town meeting; fallback is passing over to November, which DLS reportedly says can still affect FY2025.
Board will route Carl Luck's questions to contractors or town staff and post answers, including a possible exemptions section on the website.
Chair suggested forming a neighborhood re-evaluation team (board member, assessor's office, a lake resident, a non-lake resident, an objective outsider); Sarah Camer expressed interest; not voted.
Approval of minutes postponed to the next meeting when all are in the room.
Next meeting set for April 22; chair to find a room.
Once the town manager's response on tax bill timing is ready, the board will post abatement and exemption deadline information to the assessors' website and news page.

why_it_matters: The article would change a senior property tax exemption, so an older homeowner may be asked to vote on it at May town meeting, with eligibility limits that were still unsettled at this meeting.
Delayed tax bills can compress the window to file for an abatement or exemption, and the board says it will post the deadlines.
watch_next: The April 22 Board of Assessors meeting, where the minutes approval was postponed.
The May town meeting vote on the Clause 41C article, or a pass-over to a November session.
